action: Government and health bodies: enforce multi-factor authentication on file-sharing platforms, reset credentials after any unauthorised access and audit servers. No action needed for the public; services are unaffected.
exec: A national health ministry had a file-sharing platform accessed by an intruder, a reminder that auxiliary document systems are targets even when core databases are safe.
impact: Unauthorised access to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one Health Ministry facility; main databases not encrypted; health services unaffected. Amount of data accessed not stated.
plain: Malaysia's Health Ministry said someone broke into a file-sharing system at one of its facilities. Health services and treatment are continuing as normal.
summary: Malaysia's Health Ministry reported on 14 November that an intruder gained unauthorised access on 12 November to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one of its facilities. Its incident response team found the main databases were not encrypted. It blocked public access, reset passwords, audited servers and enforced multi-factor authentication. The facility, attacker and data volume were not disclosed.
title: Malaysia Health Ministry reports unauthorised access to file-sharing platform

validation.note: Single outlet; the ministry statement itself was not read.

review.note: Compared with NST 14 Nov: incident 12 Nov, supporting file platform, no database encryption, containment measures
